title: introduce-init-gate-probe-and-rollback-fence-values-for-private-installer-helm
author: Priya Kulkarni
release_notes: Adds configurable init gating probe and a namespaced rollback fence to the Private Helm chart. Improves upgrade safety by preventing cluster-wide rollbacks while tenant init sequences are in-flight. Includes values schema, templating helpers, docs, and a migration note.
description:
Motivation: Upgrades for Private installs can trigger rollbacks before tenant-scoped init jobs or preflight checks complete, causing partial state and manual recovery work. This PR introduces an opt-in init gating probe that delays marking the chart as ready until critical init jobs (DB migrations, secret bootstrap, tenant schema) report success, plus a namespaced rollback fence annotation that prevents Helm/Tiller-style rollbacks from proceeding until the fence is cleared.

What this changes: added values.privateInit.gatingProbe config (enabled, successThreshold, timeoutSeconds, checkEndpoints) and values.rollbackFence (enabled, annotationKey, gracePeriodSeconds). Templating helpers in templates/_helpers.tpl expose functions to attach the probe to initJob and the rollback fence annotation to Namespaces and Release-level resources. Also added a migration note in NOTES.txt and upgrade example in README for private-installer values.

Behavior: when privateInit.gatingProbe.enabled=true the chart renders an init-gate ConfigMap + a small probe job that queries configured endpoints (k8s readiness endpoints for migration jobs, or a simple HTTP/exec check). The Job must succeed before the Chart marks the release as fully ready. The rollbackFence, when enabled, annotates target namespaces and a controller ConfigMap with a fence timestamp; the Helm pre-rollback hook checks the fence and aborts if within gracePeriodSeconds. The fence is namespaced (does not affect other tenants) and clears automatically after successful completion or can be manually cleared via kubectl annotate.

Compatibility and opt-in: defaults are conservative (both features disabled). Existing installs are unaffected unless operators opt-in in their values.yaml. The fence uses a clear annotation name to avoid collision with other tooling.

Files changed (high level): values.schema.json updated with new fields and descriptions, templates/init-gate-job.yaml, templates/rollback-fence-hook.yaml, templates/_helpers.tpl extended, NOTES.txt and README-private.md upgrade section, chart tests (helm-unittest) updated to cover gating and fence templates.

Testing: unit template tests cover the helper functions and rendered annotations. CI ran chart lint + helm-unittest; an e2e in our staging cluster exhibited a flaky timing race which was fixed by increasing the default gatingProbe.timeoutSeconds to 600 and re-running. Manual upgrade tests performed against a multi-tenant private cluster (3 tenants) verified that enabling the probe prevented premature completion and that the rollback fence blocked rollback during the fence window.

Migration notes: operators who want the gate/fence should set values.privateInit.gatingProbe.enabled and/or values.rollbackFence.enabled and tune timeouts to match long-running DB migrations. There is a recommended recipe in README-private.md for transitioning during an active release.

Related Linear: ENG-1129 (upgrade safety for private installs), ENG-1180 (init job orchestration).
